issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a class named Meal (fully implemented), but the template repository does not provide Meal; instead it contains an Order class with the same structure and an empty Meal.java. This class-name/type mismatch will confuse students about which class to use and prevents them from following the specification (tests and problem text refer to Meal).
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a Meal class in the template matching the specification (or rename the existing Order class to Meal). Remove or update the Order class so the template and problem statement consistently refer to Meal. Also update commented usage in Main to reference Meal as in the problem statement.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution use the class name 'Meal' for the core order entity, while the template repository provides an 'Order' class with the same structure (name and ingredients). This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual entity (a single meal order) forces students to map between 'Meal' and 'Order', creating unnecessary confusion and making it unclear where to implement or extend functionality required by the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier across artifacts. Rename the template's Order class to Meal (and update its filename and all references such as in Main and comments) so it matches the problem statement and solution. Alternatively, update the problem statement to consistently use 'Order' instead of 'Meal'—prefer the first option to match the provided solution.
